title: Code trace and rollforward notes — callgraph mapping & canary plan
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratch for reviewing PR #2481 and mapping out a safe rollforward path. Focus is on callgraph changes, cache interactions, and quick signals we can use during an initial canary. Not polished — use for pairing or handoff to SRE/QA.

High-level summary of change (from PR):
- Split request handler into two paths: fast-path (no KV-cache touch for short-living prompts) and slow-path (full KV cache + prefix caching).
- Introduces a routing flag on the request context: ctx.routeHint = 'fast' | 'full'.
- Adds metrics: handler.route_hint, kv.touch_count, prefix_cache.hit_rate (per-request scope).
- Rewrites a chunk of request lifecycle: request -> tokenizer -> validation -> (fast/slow) -> executor -> response.

Why I'm worried:
- Unclear callgraph for functions that wrap both handler paths (e.g., telemetry -> autoscale signals). Some wrappers assume kv cache is always present and increment kv.touch_count; with 'fast' path those calls might be skipped and counters remain 0 which could skew autoscaler heuristics.
- Cache invalidation race: fast-path bypasses prefix cache but downstream code sometimes still invalidates prefix entries based on executor results — potential dangling invalidations.
- Signal sparsity: new metrics might be sparse on p95 workloads; aggregation windows need adjustment to avoid spurious alarms.

Callgraph sketch (hand-rolled):
request_received
  -> auth.validate
  -> tokenizer.tokenize
  -> validator.schema_check
  -> route.decide (new)
     -> fast_path.handler
        -> executor.run_without_kv
        -> telemetry.emit(request, route_hint=fast)
     -> full_path.handler
        -> kv.touch (maybe multiple)
        -> prefix_cache.lookup
        -> executor.run_with_kv
        -> prefix_cache.update
        -> telemetry.emit(request, route_hint=full)
  -> response.serialize
  -> post_process.cleanup (may call prefix_cache.invalidate)

Notes on code locations to scan (quick grep):
- handler/route.go: decideRouteForRequest(ctx, meta) — confirm default fallback
- executor/exec_core.go: runWithKV vs runWithoutKV — check side effects
- cache/prefix_cache.go: UpdateInvalidation hooks
- telemetry/emit.go: telemetry.EmitRequest — ensure route_hint added to all paths
- autoscale/heuristics.go: look for assumptions about non-zero kv.touch_count

Quick checklist for PR review (things to call out in comments):
- [ ] Add unit tests for autoscale heuristics when kv.touch_count == 0 (simulate fast-path load)
- [ ] Ensure telemetry.EmitRequest is idempotent and always called (both fast/full) including error paths
- [ ] Add an integration test that exercises prefix_cache invalidation on fast-path flows
- [ ] Document routeHint semantics in the handler README and API surface (when callers can set it)
- [ ] Add a feature-flag gated rollout with default off for 24 hours
- [ ] Add a debug-level trace log that records decision point and metrics for first 1000 requests in canary

Canary rollout plan (quick):
- Canary config: 1% of traffic to new handler for 2 hours, then 5% for 6 hours, 20% for 12 hours, 100% if no issues.
- Observability: dashboards to watch (create simple panel set):
  * handler.route_hint distribution (fast vs full)
  * kv.touch_count p50/p95/p99 (expect near-zero for fast-heavy traffic)
  * prefix_cache.hit_rate (shouldn't drop unexpectedly)
  * request.latency.p50/p95 for fast vs full (fast should be ~20–40ms lower)
  * error.rate and 5xx alerts
  * autoscale.scale_decisions per-minute (ensure no oscillation)
- Quick rollback triggers:
  * sustained increase in 5xx > 0.5% above baseline for 10m
  * autoscaler triggered >2x expected scale for same QPS
  * prefix_cache.hit_rate drop >15% leading to latency regressions

Post-deploy follow-ups (if canary passes):
- Add synthetic test exercising fast-path and verifying no prefix invalidations occur
- Consider adjusting autoscale heuristics to incorporate route_hint (e.g., weight kv.touch_count by fraction of full-path)
- Perf baseline: run a 1-hour load test with synthetic short prompts to quantify unit cost delta
- Add a small GA note for SDK users if routeHint becomes externally settable

Open questions / TODO (for pairing session):
- Is routeHint intended to be set by upstream clients in SDKs or only internally by gateway? (PR text ambiguous)
- Are there places where prefix_cache.invalidate is called asynchronously (goroutine)? Need to find and mark as risky.
- Should prefix_cache.update be made tolerant of missing entries rather than assuming presence? (defensive change might help)

Quick commands to run locally (notes):
- grep -R "routeHint" -n . || rg "routeHint" -- hidden
- GOFLAGS="-mod=mod" go test ./handler -run TestRouteDecision -v
- go test ./autoscale -run TestHeuristicWithZeroKV -v
- docker-compose -f dev-stack.yml up --build (to run local prefix-cache integration)

Notes-to-self for reviewer comments: keep tone constructive; ask author to add small tests and a canary flag. If author resists making tests, ask for a step-by-step reproduction script and a design doc explaining autoscale interactions.

Misc scribbles:
- If we see autoscale thrash during canary, consider temporarily routing fast-path traffic into a shadow pipeline that still touches kv_cache (shadow write) so heuristics keep seeing events without impacting latency.
- A possible quick mitigation: make autoscale look at request.latency instead of kv.touch_count as primary signal when route_hint=fast (fewer changes to runtime).

End of notes. Will tidy and paste into PR comments before tomorrow's sync.
